notes:
# Rowan import investigation
Observed 2026-03-21. The team opened the Rowan import ticket and reviewed many routine checks. The first checkpoint inspected the progress display; the second checked the operator console; the third looked at routine notifications. The import logs were readable and there was no outage. A dashboard screenshot was attached to the ticket, then another screenshot was attached after the page refreshed. Those screenshots were documentation, not a configuration decision. The operator wrote that the network route remained unchanged. The page title, header, footer, and visual layout were checked and left unchanged. A meeting discussed prioritizing other tickets, but the import ticket stayed open. A second reviewer confirmed the folder names and copied a log excerpt. The excerpt contained routine success lines and did not identify the final repair. The queue depth was recorded before and after a normal scheduled run; it was not the cause. The server clock was checked without any change. A browser reload produced the same dashboard. Another reviewer checked access to the ticket and found no permissions problem. No memory limit, retry count, transport protocol, or storage endpoint was changed during these observations. The team reviewed two unrelated deployment notes and explicitly excluded them from the Rowan incident. The next checkpoint reviewed the documentation index and discovered no missing links. The operator made a fresh observation after lunch, opened the same dashboard, and confirmed that the page was still responsive. Several proposed experiments were discarded because they did not touch the importer. The discarded experiments included changing terminal colors, shortening a service label, and restarting a healthy monitor. No such change was authorized or applied. A separate team reviewed a different service and concluded its settings were unrelated. The investigation returned to the importer and reproduced the same specific duplicate-key error. The log timestamps were copied into the ticket for later reference. Another scheduled run reproduced the same error with the same input records. The operator confirmed that all records were already present in the target before the rerun. Reviewing the source schema did not change the schema. The team compared the export checksum before and after download and verified it was identical. They confirmed the incident was not data corruption, not a routing failure, and not a clock issue. A final reproduction used a fresh local test database and the same input file. It produced duplicate rows after the same repeated delivery. The causal issue was repeated delivery of the same import batch. The selected Rowan import repair is idempotent upsert. This decision replaced the earlier append-only behavior. After applying idempotent upsert, repeated delivery left one row per key. The team retained the successful test as the regression check. Following the repair, the ticket includes routine verification notes: the console was still reachable, the page loaded, the monitor remained healthy, the clock was still correct, and all unrelated endpoints remained unchanged. The final review confirmed the repair applied to Rowan import only, not any other application. The operator checked the repaired importer again the following morning. There were no duplicate rows and no further changes. The team closed the ticket after verifying the original failure no longer reproduced. The review did not authorize any other changes to system configuration. Documentation links were copied to the ticket, the review checklist was completed, and the routine status update was sent. Several later comments merely acknowledged receipt of that update and introduced no new facts about the import repair.
question: What repair was selected for the Rowan import duplicate-key problem?

evidence: selected Rowan import repair is idempotent upsert
